newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 23.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
CONGRESS ASKED TO REVEAL PLANS

Rattled by the developments in the Congress, senior United Front (UF) ministers have got in touch with Congress president Sitaram Kesri to know his future plans. Sources close to Kesri have said the Congress chief has no immediate plans to ask the Congress Working Committee to withdraw support from the UF government. The apprehension among the UF ministers about their future is contrary to Prime Minister Deve Gowda's assertion that there is no threat to his government. It is also contrary to the UF leaders' public statements that although they are keenly watching the power struggle, they are not unduly perturbed over its implications.
The Times Of India
FORMER HARYANA CHIEF MINISTER'S HOUSE RAIDED

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) raided houses of former Haryana chief minister Bhajan Lal in connection with his alleged role in a bribery case. The case involves the bribing of Jharkhand Mukti Morcha leaders to vote against the no-confidence motion brought against Congress government in July 1993. Sources said the CBI recovered 1.7 million rupees in cash and jewellery worth about 2.5 million rupees from the Chandigarh residence of Bhajan Lal. The former chief minister had not, however, been arrested so far, sources added.
The Economic Times
HUGHES-ISPAT, BHARTI LOI DECISION TODAY

The Telecommunication Commission would meet on Monday to decide the award of Letter of Intent for operating basic services in Karnataka to Hughes Ispat and in Madhya Pradesh to Bharti Telenet. The Rajasthan circle has not been referred to the Commission as the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) is waiting for the law minister's opinion on the matter. The DoT has made it clear that the two circles would not be sent to the Cabinet committee for approval.
Financial Express
IT'S TIME TO PICK UP: JAMES CAPEL

Higher rural incomes and recent cut in the cash reserve ratio (CRR) by the Reserve Bank of India are likely to drive demand growth and spur investment activity in the economy. This was stated by James Capel B&K in its study. The study said the recent CRR cut would lead to a fall in interest rates apart from increasing consumption expenditure. While these factors would help the economy in the short term, long-term concerns like infrastructure bottlenecks and lack of political consensus would continue to remain a hinderance, the stock brokerage firm said.
INFLATION MOVES UP TO 6.88 PCT

The annual rate of inflation continued its steady but slow upward climb. It gained 0.08 percentage points to touch 6.88 percent for the week ended December 7. The wholesale prices index (WPI), however, witnessed a decline for the third consecutive week. The official WPI (provisional) for all commodities declined to 318.6 as against 318.8 for the previous week.
APEX BANK EASES NORMS FOR CONSORTIUM ADVANCES

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has decided to abolish the practice of uniform classification of consortium advances. The consortium members would now be given the freedom to classify advances depending on the operations in their accounts and provide for them accordingly. Earlier they had to adopt a collective stance on the quality of assets. The RBI decided to tighten the norms by directing the banks to classify a potentially sticky account as loss asset even though the corporate had not defaulted in the payment of interest and principal for two quarters.
The Observer
PLAN PANEL ALLOWS OIL COMPANIES TO FORM CONSORTIUM

The Planning Commission has accepted the petroleum and natural gas ministry's proposal to allow state-owned oil companies to form a consortium for oil and gas exploration in the country. The ministry's proposal envisages a consortium of corporates such as Oil and Natural Gas Corporation, Indian Oil Corporation, Hindustan Petroleum Corporation, Bharat Petroleum Corporation, Gas Authority of India and Oil India Ltd. Official sources say the companies would begin the process of forming the consortium next year in close collaboration with Japanese national oil companies provided the proposal is okayed by the National Development Council.
STATES CAN CLEAR PROJECTS UP TO 250 MW

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said state governments would be allowed to clear projects that could generate upto 250 mw of power. He said the federal government had sanctioned projects with a total cost of four billion rupees in the power sector during the last six months. Gowda said the decentralisation was aimed at solving an acute power shortage being faced by the states. He added that though states would be permitted to clear such power projects, their planning, distribution and displacement aspects would be monitored by the centre.
Business Line
OPTIONS TO STREAMLINE BANK PROBES BEING STUDIED

The government is considering setting up a panel to look into cases of alleged irregularities against bankers. The proposed body would be set up as a separate panel within the Reserve Bank of India and would investigate cases prior to their being referred to the investigation agencies. Official sources said the setting up of such a body would be aimed at putting in place a credible institutional arrangement to tackle growing complaints from banks over the excessive interference of investigation agencies in bank affairs.
